title: Humility & Service
subtitle: Humility is not thinking less of yourself. It is thinking about yourself less.
objectives: Explain what happened in John 13 and why it was shocking
Explain Philippians 2:3-7 and what Jesus gave up
Explain Mark 10:45 in your own words
Explain why Matthew 6 tells you not to announce it
Explain the widow's offering in Mark 12

cards.title: The lowest job in the room
cards.text: Washing feet was the work of the least important servant in a household. In John 13 the teacher does it.

cards.title: Service, with the reference
cards.text: Tap through. You will be asked for at least two of these references.

cards.title: Why Peter objected
cards.text: Peter refuses at first, and his refusal makes sense. The order of the room had just been broken in front of everybody.
points: **A household servant did this**, not the host.
**'Unless I wash you, you have no part with me.'**

question.text: Why was washing feet shocking when Jesus did it?
options: It was the job of the lowest servant in the household
Nobody had ever done it before
question.explain: That is why Peter objected. The order of the room had been broken in front of everyone.

cards.title: 'Value others above yourselves'
cards.text: Paul then describes Jesus refusing to cling to equality with God. He took the nature of a servant instead.
points: **The example is a downward move**, on purpose.

cards.title: The best fighter in a gym carries the pads
cards.text: In a good gym, the person with the record still sets out the equipment. Nobody has to ask, and everybody notices.
points: **Rank does not exempt you** from the work.
**A gym where it does** is a bad gym.
**Doing the small job** is the demonstration.

question.text: Philippians 2 describes Jesus holding on to his status.
question.explain: The opposite. He did not use equality with God to his own advantage, and took the nature of a servant.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is quiet giving and the widow's offering. Take a moment.

cards.title: Do not let your left hand know
cards.text: Matthew 6 says to give without announcing it. The instruction is odd until you ask what announcing it does.

cards.title: Announcing it changes what it was
cards.text: If you tell everyone, you have already been paid. The verse says exactly that: they have received their reward in full.
points: **'They have received their reward in full.'**
**Quiet is not modesty.** It is keeping the point.

cards.title: Helping a new player is not a highlight clip
cards.text: Somebody who stops to teach a beginner is doing something that will never appear in a montage. That is the whole reason it counts.
points: **The new player remembers it** for months.

cards.title: The widow gave two very small coins
cards.text: Wealthy people put in large amounts. Jesus says she gave more than all of them, because she gave everything she had.
points: **The measure is what it cost**, not the total.

question.text: Why did Jesus say the widow gave more than the wealthy givers?
options: She gave everything she had, out of her poverty
question.explain: The measure is what it cost the giver, not the size of the amount.

cards.title: Humility is not thinking badly of yourself
cards.text: Someone who insults himself constantly is still talking about himself. Humility takes your attention off you entirely.
points: **Not pretending you are bad at something.**

terms.def: Jesus washes the disciples' feet, the lowest servant's job.
Value others above yourselves. He made himself nothing.
He came not to be served but to serve.
Give quietly. Announcing it means the reward is already received.
The widow's two coins. The measure is what it cost her.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **John 13:** the teacher takes the servant's job.
**Mark 12:** the measure is the cost, not the amount.

quiz.text: Whose job was foot washing in a household?
quiz.explain: That is why the room went quiet and why Peter objected.
quiz.objective: Explain what happened in John 13 and why it was shocking

quiz.text: What did Peter say when Jesus came to wash his feet?
options: You will never wash my feet
quiz.explain: The answer was: unless I wash you, you have no part with me.
quiz.objective: Explain what happened in John 13 and why it was shocking

quiz.text: What does Philippians 2:3 tell you to do?
options: Give a tenth of what you have
quiz.explain: And to do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit.
quiz.objective: Explain Philippians 2:3-7 and what Jesus gave up

quiz.text: According to Philippians 2, what did Jesus do with his status?
options: He did not use it to his own advantage, and took a servant's nature
He passed it to the disciples
He kept it hidden until the end
quiz.explain: The example is a deliberate downward move. He made himself nothing.
quiz.objective: Explain Philippians 2:3-7 and what Jesus gave up

options: He came not to be served but to serve
He came to judge the nations
He came to build a temple
quiz.explain: And to give his life as a ransom for many.
quiz.objective: Explain Mark 10:45 in your own words

quiz.text: Mark 10:45 presents serving as beneath someone with authority.
quiz.explain: False. It presents serving as what the person with the most authority came to do.
quiz.objective: Explain Mark 10:45 in your own words

options: Doing good deeds in order to be seen
quiz.explain: If you announce it, you have already received your reward in full.
quiz.objective: Explain why Matthew 6 tells you not to announce it

quiz.text: What changes when you announce a good deed?
quiz.explain: The act stays the same. Its purpose is what changes.
quiz.objective: Explain why Matthew 6 tells you not to announce it

quiz.text: What did the widow in Mark 12 put into the treasury?
quiz.explain: And Jesus said she had given more than all the others.
quiz.objective: Explain the widow's offering in Mark 12

quiz.text: Why did her gift count for more?
options: The others gave from surplus; she gave everything she had
She gave more often than they did
quiz.explain: The measure is what it cost the giver, not the total handed over.
quiz.objective: Explain the widow's offering in Mark 12

quiz.text: What is humility, according to this lesson?
options: Thinking about yourself less, rather than thinking badly of yourself
quiz.explain: Someone who insults himself constantly is still talking about himself.
quiz.objective: Explain Mark 10:45 in your own words

quiz.text: Pretending to be bad at something is a form of humility.
quiz.explain: False. Humility is being accurate about yourself and then giving your attention to someone else.
quiz.objective: Explain Mark 10:45 in your own words

teacher.summary: Week 9 covers humility and service. The definition offered — thinking about yourself less rather than thinking less of yourself — is the one worth him carrying, because the alternative encourages a kind of performed self-deprecation that is still self-focused. John 13 is explained with the social detail that makes it land: foot washing was the lowest servant's job, which is why Peter objected rather than being merely embarrassed. Matthew 6 is handled as a question of purpose rather than of modesty, and the widow's offering supplies the measure: cost to the giver, not size of the gift.
discussion: Ask why Peter's objection makes sense once you know whose job foot washing was.
Ask what changes about a good deed when it is announced, and what does not.
Ask him to name a job at home nobody wants, and who usually does it.
Ask what the widow's story says about comparing gifts by size.
teacher.extension: Have him do one useful thing this week that nobody will find out about, and not tell anyone including you. The lesson is in whether he can leave it alone.
misconceptions: 'Humility means thinking you are bad at things.' It means being accurate and then looking outward.
'Jesus washing feet was just a kind gesture.' It broke the room's social order, which is why Peter objected.
'Matthew 6 forbids anyone knowing.' It addresses purpose: doing it to be seen collects the reward immediately.
'The biggest gift helps most.' Mark 12 measures the cost to the giver, not the total.
